title: Sticky
wrapsNative: LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders]) for headers that pin while scrolling; safeAreaInset(edge:content:) for a bar fixed to an edge
summary: Pinned section headers and safe-area insets, both standard SwiftUI. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Use pinnedViews when a section header should stay at the top while its section scrolls under it. Use safeAreaInset for a filter bar or an action bar that is always at the top or bottom of a scroll view; the content is inset so nothing is hidden behind it.
whenNotToUse: For the title and actions of a screen use the navigation bar and toolbar, which the system already keeps in place. In a List, section headers pin on their own in the plain style.
api: LazyVStack(alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, pinnedViews: PinnedScrollableViews = .init(), content: () -> Content)
func safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, content: () -> some View) -> some View

states.name: pinned
states.description: A section header stays at the top edge of the scroll view until the next header pushes it away.

states.name: inset bar
states.description: The bar stays at its edge and the scroll content ends above or below it.

appearance: A pinned header needs an opaque background, or the rows show through it: use a background role of the theme such as bgSurface. For a bar in a safe-area inset, the system bar material follows the light and dark appearance.
platformNotes: The web Sticky pins any element to the top or bottom with an offset, adds a shadow when stuck (elevateWhenStuck) and reports it (onStuckChange). On iOS the two cases are separate APIs: pinnedViews for headers and footers of a lazy stack, safeAreaInset for a bar that never scrolls. There is no stuck signal on iOS 17. A header that must change when pinned reads its own position with a GeometryReader in the scroll view's coordinate space, or, from iOS 18, uses onScrollGeometryChange. The web's offset is the safe area, which the system applies. Android uses stickyHeader in LazyColumn.
accessibility: Pinned headers stay in the reading order at the start of their section; mark them with the header trait.
A bar in a safe-area inset is read after the scroll content for the bottom edge and before it for the top edge.
System behaviour: the scroll content is inset by the bar, so VoiceOver focus is never behind it.
edgeCases: pinnedViews works in LazyVStack, LazyHStack and the lazy grids, not in VStack.
A pinned header without a background is drawn over the rows.
safeAreaInset on a view that does not scroll only moves the content.

parityExceptions.reason: Platform limit, system control used: SwiftUI pinned section headers give no callback when a header is pinned, so the label cannot switch from In place to Pinned.
